<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line" lang="en">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:120%;">NVIDIA</span>
</span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Visual creation demands expressive imagery together with precise control over text, layout, and structure. We introduce Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that connects these capabilities through <em id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Pixel as Code</em>. Raster images are represented by learned discrete visual tokens, while structured artifacts use explicit programs. A shared generation-and-rendering interface connects these representations to visual feedback across images, vector graphics, webpages, and documents. A Nemotron-native harness coordinates planning and raster candidate selection, with targeted repair for editable structured and hybrid artifacts. To support this interface, we develop Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer, the autoregressive raster generator Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B, and the structured-code model family Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode. On approximately 178K images spanning six visual domains, our tokenizer improves reconstruction PSNR from 26.08 to 29.57 dB over Emu3.5 IBQ. It also provides <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="7.13\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.13</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.13\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster encoding and <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="10.93\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10.93</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.93\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster decoding at batch size one on A100. In standalone evaluation, one Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode variant surpasses Kimi K3.1 Pro on the aggregate across Chart2Code, MMSVG, Design2Code, and Image2Struct. At the system level, the Nemotron-native configuration raises GenEval2 Soft-TIFA GM from 31.71 to 52.56 using the same raster generator. With our best setting, Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation achieves performance competitive with GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro across most benchmarks with available comparisons.</p>
    
<p id="abstract1.2" class="ltx_p"><a href="https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href"><span class="ltx_text" style="position:relative; bottom:-2.8pt;"><img src="2611.31358v1/assets/huggingface-logo.png" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:20/20;" width="20" height="20" alt="[Uncaptioned image]"></span>  <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#00008C;">https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B</span></a></p>
  
</div>

<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Visual creation spans photographs, illustrations, charts, webpages, posters, scientific figures, and slides. A single request may demand expressive imagery, exact wording, factual accuracy, spatial relationships, and an editable deliverable. Meeting these needs calls for both expressive synthesis and explicit control over content and structure, coordinated through representation, rendering, and visual inspection.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recent work provides complementary foundations. Edify Image <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib78" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, Sana <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib119" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and PixelDiT2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib128" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2026</a>)</cite> explore representations and architectures for image synthesis, while Cosmos 3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib74" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA, 2026a</a>)</cite> integrates multimodal understanding and generation. Agentic image creation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026b</a>)</cite> and scene-generation systems <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib118" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xia et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ling et al., 2026</a>)</cite> investigate planning, tool use, and visual assessment. These directions motivate a common interface for coordinating learned visual generation and explicit artifact structure.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pixel as Code</span>, a shared interface in which generators predict discrete representations and renderers produce visual outputs for inspection (Figure <a href="#S0.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). Learned visual tokens capture raster appearance and are decoded into pixels. Explicit programs—including SVG, HTML/CSS, plotting code, and document markup—expose content, geometry, and layout for direct editing through their respective rendering backends. Hybrid artifacts combine these complementary representations, for example by embedding a generated image within an editable webpage.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Building on this interface, we present <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation</span>. Its harness coordinates semantic planning, raster generation, and visual selection. Structured and hybrid requests additionally establish a layout contract and produce editable representations. For browser-based artifacts, visual audits assign failures to causal owners for targeted repair and checkpoint selection; native formats use their corresponding generation and review workflows. Figures <a href="#S0.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> and <a href="#S0.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> illustrate representative outputs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Our contributions span the creation interface, its learned components, and their evaluation:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">A shared interface for agentic visual creation.</span> We formulate Pixel as Code around a common <em id="S1.p6.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">generate representation <math id="S1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> render <math id="S1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> inspect</em> interface and describe how a Nemotron-native harness coordinates planning, generation, visual selection, and route-specific refinement. The browser-based workflow makes rendered feedback actionable through a resolved layout contract, explicit repair ownership, and checkpoint retention (Section <a href="#S2" title="2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Complementary models for raster and structured generation.</span> We develop Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer as the discrete raster interface, adapt Nemotron 3 Nano into the autoregressive generator Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B through multistage mid-training and reinforcement learning, and develop Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode as a family of specialized models for explicit programs and markup. Sections <a href="#S4" title="4 Training Data ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#S5" title="5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> describe the data and training, with coding variants introduced in Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Structured Code Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Evaluation from reconstruction to complete creation systems.</span> We assess tokenizer reconstruction across six visual domains, raster generation across five capability categories, and structured code generation across five tasks. One Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode variant leads the task-balanced aggregate among models evaluated on all five tasks: Chart2Code, MMSVG image-to-SVG and text-to-SVG, Design2Code, and Image2Struct. It surpasses Kimi K3.1 Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib66" title="" class="ltx_ref">Moonshot AI, 2026</a>)</cite> with fewer total and active parameters (Section <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a>). At the system level, the Nemotron-native configuration raises GenEval2 Soft-TIFA GM from 31.71 to 52.56 and WISE Verified from 46.30 to 88.60 with the same raster generator. With our best setting, the framework is competitive with GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro across most benchmarks with available comparisons.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Overall Framework</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation turns a user request and optional references into raster images or editable structured artifacts. Routing selects the artifact family, target surface, representation, and visual-asset policy. Direct raster requests use candidate generation and visual selection. Structured and hybrid requests additionally establish a layout contract, generate executable representations, and support targeted repair before checkpoint selection. The shared <span id="S2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pixel as Code</span> interface connects these routes through generation, rendering, and visual inspection. Figure <a href="#S2.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows their control flow and model assignments; Section <a href="#S3" title="3 System Components ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> describes the components and rendering backends.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F5" class="ltx_figure">
<div id="S2.F5.3" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:219.2pt;vertical-align:-0.0pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-55.7pt,35.4pt) scale(0.8,0.8) ;">

</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S2.F5.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Route-specific control flow in the Nemotron-native creation harness. Ultra denotes Nemotron 3 Ultra, Super-VL denotes Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL, and Image denotes Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B. Direct raster outputs use visual candidate selection. Browser artifacts use the Dual Coder and a bounded repair loop; repairs may update assets, the plan, or code according to the diagnosed cause. Native formats use their own generation and review workflows. Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode is evaluated separately in Section <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Pixel as Code: Discrete Representations and Renderers</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> denote the user request, <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> optional reference material, and <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> the chosen representation. Visual creation produces a discrete representation <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> and a rendered view <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{I}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>I</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{I}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="c_{r}\sim G_{r}(\,\cdot\mid q,v),\qquad\hat{I}=R_{r}(c_{r})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>I</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{r}\sim G_{r}(\,\cdot\mid q,v),\qquad\hat{I}=R_{r}(c_{r}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> generates the representation and <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> renders it (Figure <a href="#S2.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 2.1 Pixel as Code: Discrete Representations and Renderers ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>). Here, code refers to either learned discrete visual tokens or an explicit artifact representation. This abstraction does not require all representations to share a vocabulary or renderer. Instead, it exposes a common interface through which an artifact can be executed, rendered, visually inspected, and, when its representation is editable, revised.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For the <span id="S2.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">raster image route</span>, the image tokenizer provides both the discrete representation and the rendering interface. Its encoder <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> maps an image <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math> to discrete visual tokens <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}=E(I)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>I</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}=E(I)</annotation></semantics></math>, while its decoder <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> reconstructs a raster image <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{I}=D(\mathbf{z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>I</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{I}=D(\mathbf{z})</annotation></semantics></math>. This separation between discrete representation learning and generation builds on vector-quantized autoencoders <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib104" title="" class="ltx_ref">van den Oord et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Esser et al., 2021</a>)</cite>; HART <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib99" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> further studies hybrid discrete and continuous visual representations. Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B serves as the <span id="S2.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">raster image generator</span>: it autoregressively predicts discrete visual tokens, and the tokenizer decoder acts as their learned renderer. Encoding supplies representations for reference images and training targets, whereas decoding converts generated codes into visible pixels. For a direct raster request, the rendered candidates are final artifact candidates.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For <span id="S2.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">structured routes</span>, the generated representation explicitly exposes content, geometry, and layout through formats such as SVG, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, presentation objects, document structures, or plotting programs. Corresponding SVG engines, browsers, office renderers, plotting runtimes, and document compilers convert these representations into visual evidence. Because the source representation remains accessible, localized edits can be applied after visual inspection. A <span id="S2.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">hybrid route</span> additionally embeds one or more generated raster assets within a structured artifact while preserving text, shapes, layout, and interactions in an editable representation. For browser-based artifacts, the Nemotron-native configuration assigns code generation to a Dual Coder composed of Nemotron 3 Ultra <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Blakeman et al., 2026</a>)</cite> and Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL. Native presentation, document, and SVG outputs use format-specific generators and renderers. We separately train Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode for this interface (Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Structured Code Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>) and evaluate the models in standalone tests (Section <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F6" class="ltx_figure">
<div id="S2.F6.3" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:120.1pt;vertical-align:-0.0pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-35.5pt,12.4pt) scale(0.8,0.8) ;">

<span id="S2.F6.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.F6.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_align_center ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:10.2pt;--ltx-fg-color:#243449;">

</span></span><span id="S2.F6.pic1.2.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#243449;"> Discrete</span></span>
<span id="S2.F6.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.F6.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#243449;">visual tokens <span id="S2.F6.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">z</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#664493;--ltx-fill-color:#E9E2F3;" fill="#E9E2F3" stroke="#664493" stroke-width="0.7pt"><path d="M 189.78 15.75 L 85.82 15.75 C 83.52 15.75 81.66 13.89 81.66 11.6 L 81.66 -11.6 C 81.66 -13.89 83.52 -15.75 85.82 -15.75 L 189.78 -15.75 C 192.07 -15.75 193.93 -13.89 193.93 -11.6 L 193.93 11.6 C 193.93 13.89 192.07 15.75 189.78 15.75 Z M 81.66 -15.75"></path></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#243449;--ltx-fill-color:#243449;" fill="#243449" stroke="#243449" stroke-width="0.7pt" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 88.58 -3.11)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:7.69em;--ltx-fo-height:0.63em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" height="11.07" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 8.65)" width="106.41"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S2.F6.pic1.3" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_top" style="width:7.69em;">
<span id="S2.F6.pic1.3.1" class="ltx_p"></span>
<span id="S2.F6.pic1.3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.F6.pic1.3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_align_center ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:90%;width:10.2pt;--ltx-fg-color:#243449;">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S2.F6.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The representation–renderer interface underlying the creation harness. Learned visual tokens, SVG, and HTML/CSS are discrete representations with corresponding rendering backends. All routes support visual inspection; the dashed return path denotes revision of editable structured and hybrid artifacts. Direct raster outputs use candidate selection, as shown in Figure <a href="#S2.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Agentic Creation Loop</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Prior agentic scene-generation systems combine planning with visual feedback: SAGE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib118" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xia et al., 2026</a>)</cite> coordinates generation tools and critics, and Scenethesis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ling et al., 2026</a>)</cite> integrates language-based planning, visual layout refinement, and scene judging. Our harness makes this feedback operational through a resolved layout contract, renderer-grounded evidence, a root-cause report, and explicit repair ownership (Figure <a href="#S2.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Routing and structured planning.</span>
Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL classifies each request as a natural image, structured canvas, interactive interface, multi-page document, or visual series. It jointly determines the target surface, output representation, canvas count, rendering backend, and whether generated raster assets are absent, optional, or required. Search and reference retrieval are invoked conditionally, only when external factual or visual grounding materially affects the request. Nemotron 3 Ultra then produces a semantic artifact plan. For structured and hybrid routes, this plan is resolved into a layout contract that specifies the layout mode, ordered regions, normalized bounds, component ownership, and rendering constraints.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Direct raster creation.</span>
Natural-image requests bypass structured code generation. Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B produces multiple raster candidates from the planned visual brief, optional references, and a supported aspect ratio. Acting as the multimodal judge, Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL compares the rendered candidates against the original request and retains the strongest image. This route therefore uses semantic planning and visual selection, but does not invoke the structured artifact repair loop described below.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Structured and hybrid artifact creation.</span>
Structured artifacts use explicit code or native document representations, while hybrid artifacts additionally request raster assets from Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B. In the browser-based Dual Coder configuration, Nemotron 3 Ultra and Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL independently instantiate the same frozen plan and asset manifest. Native presentation, document, and SVG routes use their corresponding format-specific generation workflows. Each candidate is executed or rendered and visually inspected before an eligible candidate is retained as the initial artifact checkpoint <math id="S2.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>. Raster generation supplies requested image content, whereas the structured representation determines how assets, text, shapes, and interactions are composed into an editable artifact.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F7" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="S2.F7.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2611.31358v1/figure_furniture_layout_repair.png" id="S2.F7.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/173;" width="476" height="173" alt="Refer to caption">

</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">

</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="S2.F7.sf3" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2611.31358v1/figure_city_chart_code_content_repair.png" id="S2.F7.sf3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/127;" width="476" height="127" alt="Refer to caption">

</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F7.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="S2.F7.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Representative examples of self-correction.
<span id="S2.F7.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#D32F2F;">Red</span> annotations identify issues in the
initial renderings, while
<span id="S2.F7.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#148044;">green</span> annotations highlight the
corresponding repairs.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S2.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Evidence-grounded visual audit and targeted repair.</span>
For browser-based artifacts, the audit combines deterministic renderer evidence with a multimodal review against the frozen request and acceptance checklist. Renderer evidence identifies failures such as execution errors, missing regions, clipping, overlap, out-of-bounds geometry, and broken interactions. Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL evaluates the visible artifact and proposes a diagnosis code, causal evidence, a confidence score, and an owner within the rendered structure. Before automatic repair is applied, the harness validates this proposal against stable artifact selectors. Native formats use their own rendering, inspection, and review workflows.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The browser-based repair workflow distinguishes the visible <em id="S2.SS2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">diagnosis</em> from the underlying <em id="S2.SS2.p6.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">repair target</em>. Diagnosis codes cover component rendering, collision, containment, spatial density, typography, color contrast, layout structure, content fidelity, visual-asset quality, and interaction behavior. Repair targets identify the responsible layer: <em id="S2.SS2.p6.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">visual plan, asset, layout, code, interaction, or content</em>. Findings associated with the same causal owner are grouped into a root-cause tree, allowing the harness to repair a shared cause while freezing unaffected pages or regions. Asset-related findings can trigger raster regeneration; planning or layout findings can trigger a localized replan; and code, interaction, or content findings are assigned to the structured generation path. Every resulting candidate is executed, rendered, audited, and compared with the retained checkpoint. The numbers of accepted repair rounds and total attempted repair cycles are bounded separately.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Checkpoint retention and output selection.</span>
For exposition, let <math id="S2.SS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{t}=(P_{t},A_{t},c_{t},\hat{I}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>I</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{t}=(P_{t},A_{t},c_{t},\hat{I}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> denote the artifact state after round <math id="S2.SS2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, comprising its plan, assets, explicit representation, and rendered view. This tuple is a conceptual summary; the implementation additionally retains the frozen checklist, deterministic inspection results, multimodal review, and repair-validation records. Best-candidate retention can be expressed as</p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{\star}_{0}=C_{0},\qquad C^{\star}_{t}=\operatorname{Select}\!\left(q,C^{\star}_{t-1},C_{t}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:2.544em;" width="2.544em"><mi>Select</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{\star}_{0}=C_{0},\qquad C^{\star}_{t}=\operatorname{Select}\!\left(q,C^{\star}_{t-1},C_{t}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p7.2" class="ltx_p">For ordinary browser-based requests, the selection operator first applies deterministic fatal-render guards and then performs a blind pairwise comparison between an eligible candidate and the incumbent using the same frozen request checklist. A tie or an insufficient-confidence decision retains the earlier incumbent. Native-format routes retain the strongest rendered candidate according to their format-specific inspection and judging criteria. The loop terminates when the audit passes, no eligible improvement is found, or the configured repair budget is exhausted. The retained checkpoint provides the editable artifact together with its rendered preview.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Implementation details.</span>
Before generation, the browser-based workflow freezes the request checklist and resolved layout contract. A candidate passes only when both deterministic rendering checks and the multimodal visual audit pass. The default harness configuration generates up to four candidates for each raster-generation job. The browser-based repair loop permits up to three accepted repairs within eight attempted repair cycles and retains the incumbent when pairwise selection returns a tie or confidence below <math id="S2.SS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.75</annotation></semantics></math>. Model and renderer assignments are summarized in Section <a href="#S3" title="3 System Components ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. The routing and review prompt contracts, retrieval policies, machine-readable
schemas, and harness control limits are documented in
Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Harness Prompt Contracts and Runtime Configuration ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Qualitative self-correction examples.</span>
Figure <a href="#S2.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 2.2 Agentic Creation Loop ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> shows three representative
before-and-after repairs. In the furniture landing page, the agent resolves
text–image overlap and restores the content hierarchy. In the FrostLine
landing page, it restores the missing visual asset and reorganizes the hero
and workflow sections. In the city-population chart, it recovers all 20 bars
together with their values, city labels, and legend entries. These examples
show how the agent translates rendered feedback into targeted edits while
preserving the unaffected parts of the design.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>System Components</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The framework combines planning, discrete representation generation, rendering, and visual inspection. We describe these component responsibilities below. Section <a href="#S4" title="4 Training Data ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> presents data for both generation routes, and Section <a href="#S5" title="5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> describes training for the image tokenizer, raster image generator, and structured code generator.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Planning and Tool Coordination</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib75" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA, 2026b</a>)</cite> first performs artifact routing, and <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron 3 Ultra</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Blakeman et al., 2026</a>)</cite> serves as the planner. Ultra turns the request and any retrieved context into a semantic plan. Structured and hybrid routes additionally resolve a layout contract with ordered regions, normalized bounds, component ownership, and rendering constraints. During repair, Ultra receives issues assigned to plan revision and updates the affected specification. Harness services supply search and reference retrieval when external grounding is needed. The shared interface in Equation <a href="#S2.E1" title="Equation 1 ‣ 2.1 Pixel as Code: Discrete Representations and Renderers ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> lets planning coordinate raster assets and explicit code within the same artifact.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Discrete Representation Generators</h3>

<section id="S3.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.2.1 </span>Raster Image Generator</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B</span> is an autoregressive raster image generator. Given text and optional source or reference images, it predicts a discrete visual-token sequence that the tokenizer decoder renders into a raster image. Training includes text-to-image generation and text-and-image-conditioned generation (TI2I) with flexible aspect ratios. TI2I covers image editing, multi-turn generation, and synthesis from one or more visual references.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The generator is initialized from Nemotron 3 Nano 30B-A3B and retains its hybrid Mamba2–Transformer MoE architecture and attention configuration <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib73" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA, 2025c</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dao and Gu, 2024</a>)</cite>. Text prompts, reference images, and target images are represented as discrete tokens within a unified causal sequence. Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> describes its multistage mid-training and reinforcement learning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.2.2 </span>Structured Code Generator</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The multimodal-coding component generates representations with explicit content and structure: plotting programs for charts, SVG from images or text, HTML/CSS from visual designs, edits to existing webpage code, and document markup. These outputs are interpreted by the corresponding rendering backends described below.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For browser-based artifacts, the <span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dual Coder</span> combines <span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron 3 Ultra</span> and <span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL</span> for code generation and code or layout repair. The two models independently materialize the same frozen plan and asset manifest, then revise the code when visual diagnosis assigns an issue to this component. Native presentation, document, and SVG routes use format-specific generation workflows.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode</span> is the model family we train and evaluate for the same structured-code interface. Its multimodal-coding supervision covers the explicit representations and editing operations needed by these tasks (Section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Structured Code Generation Data ‣ 4 Training Data ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>). Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Structured Code Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a> introduces the model variants and their base models. Section <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a> reports their standalone execution and quality results against reference models. These measurements evaluate the trained coding models; the Dual Coder is a separate harness-level model assignment.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Rendering Backends</h3>

<section id="S3.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.3.1 </span>Learned Image Renderer: Tokenizer Decoder</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The dedicated image tokenizer, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer</span>, has approximately 642M parameters and uses a fixed Leech-lattice codebook <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib135" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib136" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>. Its encoder discretizes a raster image into a compact visual-token sequence; its decoder is the learned image renderer that converts predicted tokens back to pixels. This separates prediction of the discrete representation from its visual realization.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The encoder and decoder follow a vision-transformer design <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dosovitskiy et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, each with 24 layers, a hidden width of 1,024, 16 attention heads, and an MLP ratio of 4. The tokenizer uses <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16\times 16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16\times 16</annotation></semantics></math> patches and 24-dimensional quantized embeddings with L2 normalization. Its codebook contains 196,560 normalized Leech-lattice vectors and remains fixed during training. Rotary position embeddings <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib96" title="" class="ltx_ref">Su et al., 2021</a>)</cite> use a base of 10,000. The decoder uses an output FFN with a configured dimension of 3,072 and clamps reconstructed values to <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3.3.1 Learned Image Renderer: Tokenizer Decoder ‣ 3.3 Rendering Backends ‣ 3 System Components ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> summarizes the architecture and image interface; Section <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Image Tokenizer Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a> describes the training objectives and optimization schedule.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T1" class="ltx_table">

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 Image Tokenizer Quality and Efficiency ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a> evaluates the reconstruction quality, single-image latency, and encoding/decoding throughput of this learned raster interface.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.3.2 </span>Structured Rendering Backends</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SVG engines render vector markup <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib105" title="" class="ltx_ref">W3C, 2018</a>)</cite>, browser engines render HTML/CSS/JavaScript <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib113" title="" class="ltx_ref">WHATWG, 2026</a>)</cite>, and office renderers, plotting runtimes, or document compilers render their respective representations. These backends play the same interface role as the tokenizer decoder: they map generated discrete representations to visual outputs that can be inspected. Their source representations also expose elements such as shapes, text, and layout for targeted edits. The harness executes and renders revised representations after repair and preserves artifact checkpoints for subsequent comparison.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Multimodal Perception and Evaluation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL</span> provides visual assessment and candidate selection in addition to its routing and coding roles. Direct raster requests use it to select an image. In the browser-based repair loop, its audit evaluates the rendered artifact against the frozen request checklist; the root-cause tree groups issues by causal owner for assignment to the responsible component; and pairwise selection identifies the artifact state to retain. Deterministic rendering checks and validation of artifact selectors supplement the multimodal review. Native formats use their own inspection and judging workflows. These responsibilities share rendered visual evidence but follow the route-specific control flow in Section <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Agentic Creation Loop ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Training Data</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The data pipeline follows the three trainable components of the framework: the image tokenizer learns the discrete raster representation and its renderer; Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B learns to predict visual tokens from conditioning inputs; and Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode learns to generate explicit programs and markup. We describe the data for each component in this order, following the representation–renderer interface of Section <a href="#S2" title="2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Image Tokenizer Data</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We curate an approximately <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">200M-image pool</span> from the NVCLIP image corpus <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib77" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA, n.d.</a>)</cite> through clustering, deduplication, and filtering using SigLIP 2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib102" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tschannen et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, DINOv2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib80" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oquab et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, and SSCD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib82" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pizzi et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. We train the tokenizer on approximately <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">153M images</span> from this pool.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Images provide reconstruction targets for learning the encoder and decoder described in Section <a href="#S3.SS3.SSS1" title="3.3.1 Learned Image Renderer: Tokenizer Decoder ‣ 3.3 Rendering Backends ‣ 3 System Components ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3.1</span></a>. The resulting encoder supplies discrete visual tokens for raster image generation, while the decoder renders predicted tokens back into images. Section <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Image Tokenizer Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a> details the reconstruction, perceptual, distillation, and adversarial objectives.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Raster Image Generation Data</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The raster image data pipeline combines text-to-image generation (T2I) with text-and-image-conditioned generation (TI2I). T2I conditions on a textual description; TI2I additionally conditions on one or more source or reference images. TI2I covers image editing, generation from visual references, and multi-turn generation using preceding visual context. Both task families use the image tokenizer to convert target images into the discrete visual codes predicted by the generator introduced in Section <a href="#S3.SS2.SSS1" title="3.2.1 Raster Image Generator ‣ 3.2 Discrete Representation Generators ‣ 3 System Components ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.1 </span>Text-to-Image Data</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Data Collection.</span>
The web-scale portion of our text-to-image collection contains approximately <span id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">326M image–text pairs</span>. It combines GPIC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chandrasegaran et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, Conceptual 12M (CC12M) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Changpinyo et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, CommonCatalog CC-BY and CommonCatalog CC-BY-SA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gokaslan et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, Megalith <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">madebyollin, n.d.</a>)</cite>, and WIT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib95" title="" class="ltx_ref">Srinivasan et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. Together, these collections provide broad coverage of visual concepts, web photographs, encyclopedic imagery, and visual content embedded in documents.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We supplement these sources with approximately <span id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">48M synthetic images</span> generated with Z-Image <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib131" title="" class="ltx_ref">Z-Image Team, 2025</a>)</cite>, bringing the text-to-image collection to approximately <span id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">374M examples</span> for mid-training.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Data Annotation and Filtering.</span>
We annotate images using Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, and Qwen3.5-4B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib83" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2026</a>)</cite>. We remove watermarked and low-quality images, and use Qwen3.5-397B-A17B to filter out captions that do not align with the image content.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.2 </span>Data Across Training Stages</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The raster generator uses arbitrary-resolution mid-training with progressively increasing maximum image areas of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>256</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>512</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1024^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>1024</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1024^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> pixels, allowing variable aspect ratios within each stage (Section <a href="#S5.SS2.SSS1" title="5.2.1 Multi-Stage Mid-Training ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2.1</span></a>). Reinforcement learning uses a prompt collection that is refreshed to emphasize harder semantic constraints and a broader distribution of resolutions and aspect ratios, as described in Section <a href="#S5.SS2.SSS2" title="5.2.2 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Structured Code Generation Data</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The multimodal-coding mixture contains approximately <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">4.7M effective training examples</span>, including configured sampling repetitions. It covers visual reconstruction, text-conditioned program generation, editing, and code understanding across several artifact types.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Vector-graphics and visual-program examples support SVG generation, editing, and understanding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib106" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib134" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib87" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rodriguez et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Web examples connect rendered pages to their source code and provide generation and editing supervision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib130" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yun et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib97" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Chart and visualization examples cover plotting code, structured chart representations, and program understanding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib123" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ni et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib67" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ni et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The mixture also includes formula transcription <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Blecher, 2025</a>)</cite>, table-to-<span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_LaTeX_logo" style="letter-spacing:-0.2em; margin-right:0.1em;">L<span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="position:relative; bottom:0.4ex;font-variant:small-caps;;">a</span>T<span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="position:relative; bottom:-0.2ex;font-variant:small-caps;font-size:120%;">e</span>X</span> conversion, and CAD-related supervision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib69" title="" class="ltx_ref">Niu et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, supplemented by teacher-generated chain-of-thought examples and direct ground-truth anchors. Together, these task groups connect visual appearance and user intent to the explicit representations predicted by Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode; Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Structured Code Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a> describes their use in supervised adaptation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Training</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training is organized around three components of the Pixel as Code framework. The <span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">image tokenizer</span> learns a discrete visual representation and its decoder. The <span id="S5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">raster image generator</span>, Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B, learns to predict visual tokens, and the <span id="S5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">structured code generator</span>, Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode, learns to produce explicit programs and markup from the multimodal-coding mixture in Section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Structured Code Generation Data ‣ 4 Training Data ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>. We describe their training separately in Sections <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Image Tokenizer Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>, <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>, and <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Structured Code Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>, following the component definitions in Section <a href="#S3" title="3 System Components ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Image Tokenizer Training</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The image tokenizer learns a discrete visual representation and its rendering interface from the NVCLIP images described in Section <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Image Tokenizer Data ‣ 4 Training Data ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, using the architecture in Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3.3.1 Learned Image Renderer: Tokenizer Decoder ‣ 3.3 Rendering Backends ‣ 3 System Components ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Training spans 670K steps and combines pixel reconstruction, perceptual supervision, feature distillation, and adversarial learning. The codebook remains fixed, while the encoder is frozen after 480K steps. The decoder continues to learn to reconstruct images from the resulting discrete codes.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Visual compression determines both reconstruction fidelity and the sequence budget for generation. Cosmos <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib71" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA, 2025a</a>)</cite> develops visual tokenizers for world modeling, DC-AE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> studies deep compression for high-resolution diffusion, and DC-AR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib115" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> uses a deep-compression hybrid tokenizer for masked autoregressive generation. In our tokenizer, the <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16\times 16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16\times 16</annotation></semantics></math> patch size represents a <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256\times 256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>256</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256\times 256</annotation></semantics></math> image with 256 tokens, compared with 1,024 tokens for <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8\times 8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8\times 8</annotation></semantics></math> patches. In our tokenizer study, this setting enables <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times</annotation></semantics></math> more samples per node. This trade-off connects the fidelity of the learned renderer to the sequence budget of the raster image generator.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reconstruction.</span>
We use an L1 reconstruction loss with weight 1.0 and an LPIPS perceptual loss <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib133" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2018</a>)</cite> with weight 0.1.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Decoder feature distillation.</span>
We use DINOv2 ViT-L <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib80" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oquab et al., 2023</a>)</cite> as the distillation teacher. Student features are taken from the third decoder block, projected through an MLP, and aligned to the teacher’s spatial grid using two-dimensional adaptive average pooling. Both student and teacher features are L2-normalized independently at each token. For the resulting <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> aligned token pairs <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s_{i},t_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s_{i},t_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, the distillation loss is the negative mean cosine similarity,</p>
<table id="S5.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{distill}}=-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\cos(s_{i},t_{i}),\qquad\lambda_{\mathrm{distill}}=0.1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>distill</mi></msub><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>distill</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{distill}}=-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\cos(s_{i},t_{i}),\qquad\lambda_{\mathrm{distill}}=0.1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">This auxiliary supervision acts on the learned decoder and supports arbitrary image resolutions through spatial feature alignment.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adversarial training.</span>
An unconditional PatchGAN discriminator <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Isola et al., 2017</a>)</cite> operates on RGB images with three layers, a base width of 64, <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4\times 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times 4</annotation></semantics></math> kernels, and batch normalization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ioffe and Szegedy, 2015</a>)</cite>. It uses the <span id="S5.SS1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pad_max</span> mode for arbitrary resolutions, with blur downsampling and ActNorm disabled. The GAN objective is softplus, with a configured discriminator weight of 0.5 and adaptive discriminator weighting disabled. Adversarial training starts at step 0. R1 regularization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib65" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mescheder et al., 2018</a>)</cite> uses <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=10</annotation></semantics></math> and is evaluated once every 16 steps with lazy regularization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2020</a>)</cite>. On regularization steps, the R1 penalty is multiplied by <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\gamma/2)\times 16=80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\gamma/2)\times 16=80</annotation></semantics></math>, giving a time-averaged coefficient of <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma/2=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma/2=5</annotation></semantics></math>. Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1 Image Tokenizer Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> collects these loss settings and the training configuration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Quantizer training.</span>
We keep the codebook fixed throughout training and use a straight-through estimator <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bengio et al., 2013</a>; <a href="#bib.bib104" title="" class="ltx_ref">van den Oord et al., 2017</a>)</cite> to propagate gradients through discrete quantization. The training objective does not include a commitment loss.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Variable-resolution token packing.</span>
Each image is represented as a sequence of <math id="S5.SS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16\times 16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16\times 16</annotation></semantics></math> patches. We pack sequences of different lengths into a batch while preserving image boundaries, so images retain their individual spatial resolutions without padding every sequence to a common length. Replicate padding only aligns each image to the patch grid. Batches are formed under a per-rank pixel budget of approximately 2.62M; their image count therefore varies with resolution. Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1 Image Tokenizer Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> summarizes the packing configuration.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span>Image tokenizer training configuration through 670K steps. AdamW optimizes both the tokenizer autoencoder and the discriminator; Table <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 5.1 Image Tokenizer Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> gives the effective learning rates.</figcaption>
