<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S5.T2.6.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S5.T2.6.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-top:0.45pt;padding-bottom:0.45pt;">

<span id="S5.T2.6.1.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:164.0pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.T2.6.1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Value</span></span>

</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S5.T2.6.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T2.6.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:0.45pt;padding-bottom:0.45pt;" colspan="2"><span id="S5.T2.6.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Reconstruction and distillation</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T2.6.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T2.6.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-top:0.45pt;padding-bottom:0.45pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:169.1pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.T2.6.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Pixel reconstruction / weight</span></span>
</span></td>

<td id="S5.T2.6.41.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-top:0.45pt;padding-bottom:0.45pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.41.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:169.1pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.41.1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.T2.6.41.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Encoder freezing</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="S5.T2.6.41.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-top:0.45pt;padding-bottom:0.45pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.41.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:164.0pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.41.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.T2.6.41.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">After 480K steps</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T2.6.42" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T2.6.42.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:0.45pt;padding-bottom:0.45pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.42.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:169.1pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.42.1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.T2.6.42.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Training duration</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="S5.T2.6.42.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:0.45pt;padding-bottom:0.45pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.42.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:164.0pt;">
<span id="S5.T2.6.42.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.T2.6.42.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">670K steps</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Optimization and learning-rate schedule.</span>
Both the tokenizer autoencoder and the discriminator use AdamW <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019</a>)</cite> with weight decay <math id="S5.SS1.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS1.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}=0.9</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS1.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{2}=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{2}=0.99</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S5.SS1.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon=10^{-8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon=10^{-8}</annotation></semantics></math>. Training uses BF16 automatic mixed precision and gradient checkpointing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2016</a>)</cite>. The configuration’s base learning rate is <math id="S5.SS1.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4\times 10^{-7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times 10^{-7}</annotation></semantics></math>, scaled by a world size of 32 and a nominal batch size of 8:</p>
<table id="S5.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta(t)=\eta_{\mathrm{base}}\,W\,B_{\mathrm{nom}}\,m(t)=(4\times 10^{-7})\times 32\times 8\times m(t)=1.024\times 10^{-4}\,m(t)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>base</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>W</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>nom</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>32</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1.024</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta(t)=\eta_{\mathrm{base}}\,W\,B_{\mathrm{nom}}\,m(t)=(4\times 10^{-7})\times 32\times 8\times m(t)=1.024\times 10^{-4}\,m(t),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS1.p8.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S5.SS1.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is the stage multiplier in Table <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 5.1 Image Tokenizer Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. The nominal batch size is a learning-rate scaling parameter, distinct from the number of images in each packed batch. The multiplier decreases from 1.0 to 0.6 at 300K steps and to 0.36 at 480K steps. The last stage freezes the encoder and uses a learning rate of <math id="S5.SS1.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.6864\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.6864</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.6864\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> through 670K steps.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 3</span>: </span><span id="S5.T3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Tokenizer learning-rate stages. The multiplier scales the base rate after world-size and nominal-batch-size scaling. The codebook is frozen throughout training.</span></figcaption>

<div id="S5.SS1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 Image Tokenizer Quality and Efficiency ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a> evaluates reconstruction quality, single-image latency, and encoding/decoding throughput. Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Additional Image Tokenizer Results ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a> provides domain-level reconstruction results and an ImageNet any-resolution comparison with an encoding-scale ablation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Raster Image Generator Training</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The raster generator adapts a language-pretrained backbone through multistage autoregressive mid-training, followed by on-policy reinforcement learning. Mid-training teaches visual-token prediction with progressively increasing pixel budgets; reinforcement learning optimizes the rendered outputs for semantic alignment and perceptual quality. Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 5.2.1 Multi-Stage Mid-Training ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> summarizes the stage-wise configuration. Sections <a href="#S5.SS2.SSS1" title="5.2.1 Multi-Stage Mid-Training ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2.1</span></a> and <a href="#S5.SS2.SSS2" title="5.2.2 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2.2</span></a> describe these two parts of training.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.2.1 </span>Multi-Stage Mid-Training</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We continue training the language-pretrained backbone to autoregressively predict target-image tokens from text and optional source or reference images. All three stages use 90% T2I and 10% TI2I data (Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Raster Image Generation Data ‣ 4 Training Data ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>), covering text-to-image generation, editing, and reference-conditioned synthesis. The maximum image area increases through <math id="S5.SS2.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>256</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS2.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>512</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S5.SS2.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1024^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>1024</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1024^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> pixels, with variable aspect ratios; the corresponding training durations are 35K, 90K, and 70K steps. Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 5.2.1 Multi-Stage Mid-Training ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> lists the optimization settings.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T4" class="ltx_table">
<div id="S5.T4.3" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:135.4pt;vertical-align:-66.3pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-135.5pt,53.1pt) scale(0.560141609056439,0.560141609056439) ;">
<table id="S5.T4.3.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S5.T4.3.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T4.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.75pt 7.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Configuration</span></td>
<td id="S5.T4.3.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.75pt 7.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.3.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mid-Training Stage 1</span></td>
<td id="S5.T4.3.1.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.75pt 7.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.3.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mid-Training Stage 2</span></td>
<td id="S5.T4.3.1.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.75pt 7.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.3.1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mid-Training Stage 3</span></td>
<td id="S5.T4.3.1.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.75pt 7.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.3.1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reinforcement Learning</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T4.3.1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T4.3.1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding:0.75pt 7.0pt;">Maximum image pixels</td>
<td id="S5.T4.3.1.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.75pt 7.0pt;"><math id="S5.T4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>256</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S5.T4.3.1.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.75pt 7.0pt;"><math id="S5.T4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>512</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S5.T4.3.1.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.75pt 7.0pt;"><math id="S5.T4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1024^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>1024</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1024^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S5.T4.3.1.2.5" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.75pt 7.0pt;">–</td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T4.3.1.3" class="ltx_tr">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T4.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 4</span>: </span><span id="S5.T4.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="S5.T4.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Raster image generator training configurations.</span>

stages with increasing maximum image pixel counts and the mixed-resolution
reinforcement-learning stage. Aspect ratios vary within each mid-training stage.

text and source or reference images.

<section id="S5.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.2.2 </span>Reinforcement Learning</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Reinforcement learning has been studied for both discrete autoregressive image generation, as in X-Omni <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Geng et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and diffusion models. Data-regularized RL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib126" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ye et al., 2025</a>)</cite> combines reward optimization with diffusion-based data regularization. We describe our discrete-token policy and its reward-driven training procedure below.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">From supervised learning to preference optimization.</span>
Building on multistage mid-training, we introduce reinforcement learning once high-quality, prompt-faithful candidates consistently emerge under repeated sampling. This best-of-<math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> headroom provides a strong on-policy learning signal: repeated rollouts explore new compositions of the concepts and visual patterns acquired during mid-training, while reward-guided updates consolidate successful discoveries into reliable single-sample behavior. We adopt a two-stage RL scheme: broad-coverage optimization followed by learnability-driven data refresh to sustain informative learning signals as the policy improves.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Stage I: broad-coverage RL.</span>
The first RL stage draws from a broad prompt distribution spanning object-centric generation, attribute binding, counting, spatial relations, interactions, complex scene composition, stylistic control, and text rendering. This diverse coverage encourages the policy to explore and combine its acquired visual knowledge across a wide range of generation requirements. For every prompt, the current policy generates a group of candidates and receives pointwise alignment and image-quality scores. Groups with sufficient reward variation yield informative relative advantages, providing a discriminative learning signal for group-relative policy optimization.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Stage II: learnability-driven data refresh.</span>
As Stage I proceeds, easy prompts increasingly produce uniformly strong candidates and their within-group alignment-score range contracts. We retain for GRPO only prompt groups with sufficient within-group reward variation; groups lacking a discriminative relative ordering are discarded before the policy update. The growing prevalence of low-range groups signals that the current prompt distribution no longer matches the policy’s evolving learning frontier. We therefore refresh the prompt distribution while preserving the reward definition and optimizer state. The refreshed mixture retains structured compositional prompts, redistributes general prompts across multiple resolutions and aspect ratios according to the empirical prior of our mid-training corpus, and introduces longer, more challenging prompts with denser semantic and compositional constraints. Pairing these difficult cases with diverse image geometries restores informative reward variation without changing the optimization objective. The resulting loop—<em id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p4.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">roll out, diagnose, recurate, and improve</em>—uses the model’s evolving behavior to identify which examples can still induce informative on-policy comparisons. Our two-stage RL training instantiates one iteration of this broader self-improvement process. Figure <a href="#S5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 5.2.2 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> uses representative examples to illustrate the progression from mid-training to RL alignment and the full agentic workflow. Across these examples, RL improves legible text rendering, single-object structure and surface detail, and compliance with counting and spatial relations. The complete agentic workflow further improves exact text and count fidelity, coverage of densely specified multi-object scenes, fine-grained actions and material detail, and consistency under explicit artistic styles.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F8" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<table id="S5.F8.3" class="ltx_tabular ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S5.F8.3.1" class="ltx_tr">

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We next detail the optimization procedure used to obtain the RL-aligned policy. We first formulate autoregressive image generation as a discrete-token policy, then define the pointwise reward and group-relative objective, and finally describe the rollout filtering and distributed execution used in training. We optimize the policy with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib90" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. Because trajectories are regenerated from the continually updated policy rather than drawn from a fixed preference set, successive rollout iterations explore previously unrealized combinations of the model’s acquired knowledge, while group-relative rewards determine which discoveries are reinforced by subsequent policies.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Discrete-token policy.</span>
Let <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the prompt tokens and <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}=(z_{1},\ldots,z_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}=(z_{1},\ldots,z_{T})</annotation></semantics></math> the discrete visual-token sequence generated by <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>. The tokenizer decoder renders <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{I}=D(\mathbf{z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>I</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{I}=D(\mathbf{z})</annotation></semantics></math>, instantiating Equation <a href="#S2.E1" title="Equation 1 ‣ 2.1 Pixel as Code: Discrete Representations and Renderers ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. The autoregressive policy factorizes as</p>
<table id="S5.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})=\prod_{t=1}^{T}\pi_{\theta}\!\left(z_{t}\mid\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z}_{&lt;t}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐳</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})=\prod_{t=1}^{T}\pi_{\theta}\!\left(z_{t}\mid\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z}_{&lt;t}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p6.2" class="ltx_p">This permits direct application of the token-level GRPO objective used for language models. Prompt and reference-image tokens provide context but are excluded from the action loss; the action mask selects only generated response tokens, including visual-token IDs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Composite pointwise reward.</span>
Each candidate code is rendered by the tokenizer decoder at its requested resolution and independently evaluated against the original prompt by a pointwise VLM judge. The judge scores six alignment dimensions—including counting, relations, actions, and text rendering—together with technical image quality. After aggregation and normalization to <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, we define</p>
<table id="S5.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z})=0.7\,\bar{r}_{\mathrm{align}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z})+0.3\,\bar{r}_{\mathrm{quality}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>0.7</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>align</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>0.3</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>quality</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z})=0.7\,\bar{r}_{\mathrm{align}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z})+0.3\,\bar{r}_{\mathrm{quality}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p7.2" class="ltx_p">One judge call produces both components under the same visual evidence and rubric. The complete instruction, structured output, and aggregation rule are given in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Reward-Judge Prompt and Scalarization ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Group-relative credit assignment.</span>
For each prompt, the rollout policy samples <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}(\mathbf{x})=\{\mathbf{z}^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}(\mathbf{x})=\{\mathbf{z}^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^{G}</annotation></semantics></math> and normalizes rewards within this group:</p>
<table id="S5.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{i}=\frac{R(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z}^{(i)})-\mu_{\mathcal{G}}}{\sigma_{\mathcal{G}}+\epsilon},\qquad\mathbf{z}^{(i)}\in\mathcal{G}(\mathbf{x})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{i}=\frac{R(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z}^{(i)})-\mu_{\mathcal{G}}}{\sigma_{\mathcal{G}}+\epsilon},\qquad\mathbf{z}^{(i)}\in\mathcal{G}(\mathbf{x}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{\mathcal{G}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{\mathcal{G}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\mathcal{G}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\mathcal{G}}</annotation></semantics></math> are the group statistics. This removes prompt-specific score offsets, and the resulting sequence-level advantage <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is shared by all generated tokens in trajectory <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{i,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{i,t}</annotation></semantics></math> be the action mask and <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{i,t}(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{i,t}(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> the likelihood ratio between the current and rollout policies for token <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math>. The PPO-style clipped objective <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib88" title="" class="ltx_ref">Schulman et al., 2017</a>)</cite> is</p>
<table id="S5.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{split}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GRPO}}(\theta)=-\mathbb{E}_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mathbf{x}\sim\mathcal{D},\\

&amp;\operatorname{clip}(\rho_{i,t}(\theta),1-\epsilon_{\mathrm{lo}},1+\epsilon_{\mathrm{hi}})A_{i}\Big)\Bigg].\end{split}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable columnspacing="0pt" \mathbf{z}^{(i)}\sim\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}\end{subarray}}\Bigg[\frac{1}{\sum_{i,t}m_{i,t}}\sum_{i,t}m_{i,t}\min\Big(&amp;\rho_{i,t}(\theta)A_{i},\\
&amp;\operatorname{clip}(\rho_{i,t}(\theta),1-\epsilon_{\mathrm{lo}},1+\epsilon_{\mathrm{hi}})A_{i}\Big)\Bigg].\end{split}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F10" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.31358v1/rl_stage1_saturation.svg" id="S5.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:390/143;" width="390" height="143"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F10.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="S5.F10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Stage I saturation diagnostics. (a) RL reward over valid images; the light and dark curves show per-iteration values and a short-window median. (b) Fraction of fully valid groups satisfying Eq. <a href="#S5.E9" title="Equation 9 ‣ 5.2.2 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>, audited every ten iterations; markers and line show the observations and their trend.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p9.1" class="ltx_p">We use <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{\mathrm{lo}}=0.20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>lo</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{\mathrm{lo}}=0.20</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{\mathrm{hi}}=0.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>hi</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.28</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{\mathrm{hi}}=0.28</annotation></semantics></math>, a learning rate of <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>, and no explicit KL penalty; Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 5.2.1 Multi-Stage Mid-Training ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> summarizes the remaining settings.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Rollout and update schedule.</span>
Each rollout iteration samples <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G=32</annotation></semantics></math> candidates at temperature 1.0 for each of <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>48</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=48</annotation></semantics></math> prompts, yielding 1,536 trajectories. Keeping prompt groups intact, we partition them into two disjoint batches of 768 trajectories and take one optimizer step per batch; every trajectory is therefore used once. Consequently, the reported 200 rollout iterations correspond to 400 optimizer steps. In pilot experiments, smaller groups produced noisy baselines and often failed to improve reward, whereas <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G=32</annotation></semantics></math> more reliably exposed meaningful within-prompt reward variation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reward-range group filtering.</span>
Before optimization, we retain a prompt group only when its alignment-score range on the original 0–10 scale satisfies</p>
<table id="S5.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max_{i\in\mathcal{G}}r_{\mathrm{align},i}-\min_{i\in\mathcal{G}}r_{\mathrm{align},i}\geq 2." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>align</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>align</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max_{i\in\mathcal{G}}r_{\mathrm{align},i}-\min_{i\in\mathcal{G}}r_{\mathrm{align},i}\geq 2.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p11.2" class="ltx_p">This removes both saturated groups whose candidates are uniformly strong and failed groups with no useful relative ordering. Rejection does not shrink the update batch: the sampler draws a new prompt and repeats generation and reward evaluation until all <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>48</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=48</annotation></semantics></math> accepted groups have been collected. The accepted-group yield therefore measures how much of the current prompt distribution still provides informative within-group comparisons.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p12.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ 5.2.2 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> isolates the dynamics of Stage I, before the prompt and resolution distribution is changed. Panel (a) reports the mean RL reward over successfully decoded images at every rollout iteration. Panel (b) audits the fraction of complete prompt groups for which all 32 candidates decode successfully and the alignment-score range satisfies Eq. <a href="#S5.E9" title="Equation 9 ‣ 5.2.2 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>. As optimization proceeds, reward rises and gradually approaches a plateau, whereas the yield of informative groups decreases. This divergence indicates that the policy is improving on the current distribution while an increasing fraction of prompts no longer produces sufficiently discriminative within-group comparisons. We use this saturation signal to motivate the Stage II data refresh described above, replacing increasingly exhausted prompts with harder semantic constraints and a broader resolution distribution.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p13" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p13.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p13.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Rollout-policy consistency.</span>
Rollouts and gradient computation use separate inference and training implementations. To suppress bias from small numerical discrepancies over long visual-token sequences, we compute the geometric-mean likelihood ratio</p>
<table id="S5.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}=\exp\!\left(\frac{1}{\sum_{t}m_{i,t}}\sum_{t}m_{i,t}\log\frac{\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(z_{t}^{(i)}\mid\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z}_{&lt;t}^{(i)})}{\pi_{\mathrm{roll}}(z_{t}^{(i)}\mid\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z}_{&lt;t}^{(i)})}\right)." lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>t</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>roll</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}=\exp\!\left(\frac{1}{\sum_{t}m_{i,t}}\sum_{t}m_{i,t}\log\frac{\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(z_{t}^{(i)}\mid\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z}_{&lt;t}^{(i)})}{\pi_{\mathrm{roll}}(z_{t}^{(i)}\mid\mathbf{x},\mathbf{z}_{&lt;t}^{(i)})}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p13.2" class="ltx_p">We retain sequences with <math id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}\in[0.95,1.05]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0.95</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.05</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}\in[0.95,1.05]</annotation></semantics></math> and apply token-level importance weights to the surviving losses.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p14" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p14.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS2.p14.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Scalable asynchronous execution.</span>
Following large-scale image RL systems <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib122" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, we decouple rollout generation, reward evaluation, and policy optimization across 256 GPUs. Disaggregated actors, inference engines, and decoding workers overlap generation with asynchronous VLM scoring. Failed scorer requests are retried; unrecoverable groups are discarded and backfilled rather than assigned artificial zero rewards. We checkpoint every 25 rollout iterations and retain complete rollout records for auditing.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Structured Code Generator Training</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train two variants of Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode. <span id="S5.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode-30B-A3B</span> is initialized from the Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B GA model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib76" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA, 2026c</a>)</cite><span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            Official Hugging Face model: <a href="https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16</a>.</span></span></span>. <span id="S5.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode-120B-A12B</span> is trained from Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib75" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA, 2026b</a>)</cite>. Both variants use the same training data and training procedure, including the supervised fine-tuning mixture and task-specific reinforcement learning described below.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We apply <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">multimodal-coding supervised fine-tuning</span> on approximately 4.7M effective training examples (Section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Structured Code Generation Data ‣ 4 Training Data ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>). The mixture covers visual reconstruction, instruction-conditioned program generation, editing, and code understanding. For generation tasks, the targets are explicit programs and markup, providing supervision for the structured generation interface <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> in Equation <a href="#S2.E1" title="Equation 1 ‣ 2.1 Pixel as Code: Discrete Representations and Renderers ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Following supervised fine-tuning, we further optimize both models with Group Relative Policy Optimization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib90" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> using task-specific rewards. We build a custom sandbox that executes Python programs, renders SVG and HTML/CSS, and compiles LaTeX for reward evaluation. This infrastructure connects generated code to its executable or rendered outputs, providing feedback on both execution validity and task-specific quality. The reward design follows the requirements of each structured-code task. Execution checks assess whether generated programs run successfully, markup renders, edits can be parsed, and documents compile. Quality scores measure visual fidelity for reconstruction, text-image alignment and aesthetics for text-to-SVG generation, and edit accuracy for code editing. These outcome-based signals complement supervised fine-tuning by rewarding functional correctness and the quality of the resulting artifacts.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate both trained variants against their respective base models using execution, compilation, rendering, and task-specific quality metrics (Section <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our evaluation follows the framework’s representation–renderer interface. We first measure image tokenizer reconstruction quality and efficiency, then evaluate raster image generation and its agent-assisted configurations by visual capability, and finally assess structured code generation through execution, rendering, and task-specific quality metrics.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Image Tokenizer Quality and Efficiency</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reconstruction quality.</span>
We evaluate the learned raster renderer on approximately 178K images spanning natural photographs, documents, charts, UI screenshots, faces, and generated or edited images. Appendix <a href="#A3.SS1" title="C.1 Evaluation Image Sources ‣ Appendix C Additional Image Tokenizer Results ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a> lists the 35 source datasets by visual domain. Table <a href="#S6.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 6.1 Image Tokenizer Quality and Efficiency ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> compares Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer with the Emu3.5 IBQ tokenizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cui et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. We report PSNR, SSIM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib112" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2004</a>)</cite>, LPIPS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib133" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2018</a>)</cite>, and GMSD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib124" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xue et al., 2013</a>)</cite> for reconstruction fidelity, together with FID <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Heusel et al., 2017</a>)</cite> and feature-distribution distance in DINOv2 space <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib80" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oquab et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. MUSIQ <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ke et al., 2021</a>)</cite> and CLIP-IQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib107" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2023</a>)</cite> assess reconstructed images without a reference.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T5" class="ltx_table">

</table>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">On the six-domain evaluation, Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer achieves 29.57 dB PSNR versus 26.08 dB for Emu3.5 IBQ, a 3.49 dB improvement (Table <a href="#S6.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 6.1 Image Tokenizer Quality and Efficiency ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). SSIM increases by 0.053, while LPIPS decreases by approximately 17% and GMSD by 32%. All six domains improve on these four fidelity metrics, with PSNR gains of 4.63–5.35 dB on documents, charts, and UI screenshots. This is particularly relevant to a renderer used within visual artifacts containing text and structured layouts. Overall FID and FD-DINOv2 also decrease, although these gains do not hold in every domain. MUSIQ and CLIP-IQA are slightly lower overall. Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Additional Image Tokenizer Results ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a> reports the domain-level results and an ImageNet any-resolution comparison with an encoding-scale ablation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Qualitative reconstruction.</span>
Figure <a href="#S6.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ 6.1 Image Tokenizer Quality and Efficiency ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> compares matched crops from selected GPIC examples <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chandrasegaran et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer more faithfully preserves thin web strands, diagram contours, and repetitive fabric texture in these examples. Both tokenizers still alter some fine details and small characters. The full input images and marked crop regions provide context for the local comparisons. Appendix <a href="#A3.SS5" title="C.5 Additional Qualitative Comparisons ‣ Appendix C Additional Image Tokenizer Results ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.5</span></a> adds eight examples spanning documents, signs, product packaging, natural textures, reflective materials, and portraits.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F11" class="ltx_figure">
<table id="S6.F11.3" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S6.F11.3.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S6.F11.3.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-bottom: 4.0pt;"><span id="S6.F11.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Input image</span></td>
<td id="S6.F11.3.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-bottom: 4.0pt;"><span id="S6.F11.3.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Original crop</span></td>
<td id="S6.F11.3.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-bottom: 4.0pt;"><span id="S6.F11.3.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Emu3.5 IBQ</span></td>
<td id="S6.F11.3.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center" style="padding-bottom: 4.0pt;">
<span id="S6.F11.3.1.4.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_middle" style="width:84.2pt;">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F11.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 11</span>: </span><span id="S6.F11.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Qualitative tokenizer reconstruction on selected GPIC images <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chandrasegaran et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. Red boxes mark the regions compared in the three crop columns. Each row uses the same <math id="S6.F11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256\times 256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>256</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256\times 256</annotation></semantics></math> region from the original image and both reconstructions, shown at the same scale. The examples illustrate fine-line continuity, diagram contours, and fabric texture; Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer uses the 670K-step checkpoint.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Encoding and decoding efficiency.</span>
The learned raster interface incurs encoding costs when preparing visual inputs and decoding costs when rendering generated codes. Figure <a href="#S6.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ 6.1 Image Tokenizer Quality and Efficiency ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> compares Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer with the Emu3.5 vision tokenizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cui et al., 2025</a>)</cite> on NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB and L4 GPUs, separating batch size 1 from larger batches. Both GPUs use BF16 and <math id="S6.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1024\times 1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1024</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1024\times 1024</annotation></semantics></math> inputs. The A100 measurements are medians over five timed runs following warmup, excluding image loading, preprocessing, and CPU-to-GPU transfer. L4 batch-size-one results use standard runs, while its largest tested batches use short runs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">At batch size 1 on A100, Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer encodes an image in 41.30 ms and decodes it in 37.10 ms, compared with 294.53 ms and 405.46 ms for Emu3.5, giving latency speedups of <math id="S6.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="7.13\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.13</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.13\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="10.93\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10.93</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.93\times</annotation></semantics></math>. On L4, Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer reaches 7.70 images/s for encoding and 8.78 images/s for decoding, compared with 0.928 and 0.675 images/s for Emu3.5, giving throughput ratios of <math id="S6.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="8.30\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.30</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.30\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="13.01\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>13.01</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13.01\times</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F12" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.31358v1/tokenizer_throughput.svg" id="S6.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/297;" width="476" height="297"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F12.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 12</span>: </span><span id="S6.F12.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Tokenizer throughput on one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB or L4 GPU, using BF16 and <math id="S6.F12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1024\times 1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1024</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1024\times 1024</annotation></semantics></math> inputs. Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer uses the 670K-step checkpoint. The upper row compares batch size 1; the lower row shows the reported peak batches on A100 and largest tested runnable batches on L4. B denotes batch size; <sup id="S6.F12.5.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S6.F12.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup> marks L4 short runs. All panels share the same linear scale. Larger L4 batches do not maximize throughput.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Larger batches improve throughput on A100: Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer encodes 29.28 images/s and decodes 32.16 images/s at batch size 16, versus 4.76 and 3.52 images/s for Emu3.5 at batch size 8, corresponding to <math id="S6.SS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="6.15\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.15</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.15\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS1.p6.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="9.14\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>9.14</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.14\times</annotation></semantics></math> higher throughput. On L4, Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer’s highest observed throughput occurs at batch size 1. Its largest tested runnable batch is 12, compared with 2 for Emu3.5 encoding and 4 for decoding; Emu3.5 runs out of memory at batch 4 for encoding and batch 8 for decoding. These measurements describe tokenizer processing; total creation time also depends on visual-token generation and the surrounding agentic workflow.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Raster Image Generation and Agentic Creation</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We organize the text-to-image suite into five categories: composition and prompt following, visual text rendering, broad visual generation, knowledge and reasoning, and commercial design. Each category has a separate table and analysis. These categories group the capabilities emphasized by the benchmarks; their overall scores are not interchangeable measures of a single ability. TI2I is included in training but has not been evaluated.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We report three configurations: direct generation with <span id="S6.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B (standalone)</span> and two versions of <span id="S6.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation</span>, labeled <span id="S6.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(+ Nemotron agentic model)</span> and <span id="S6.SS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(+ GPT-6 agentic model)</span>. Both framework configurations use the same raster image generator with their respective agent models. Their scores measure complete configurations; they do not isolate individual planning, search, inspection, or revision steps.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Comparison values are collected from official reports and leaderboards, including HiDream-O1-Image <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cai et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, UniGenBench++ <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib110" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>, ERNIE-Image <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">ERNIE-Image Team, 2026</a>)</cite>, and SenseNova-U1.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Diao et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. The comparison set includes additional models from SenseNova-U1.5 with results on at least three of the suite’s columns. Where multiple sources report the same variant and metric, we retain the lower value. Each category omits baseline rows with no reported score in that category.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">All scores retain their reported percentage scale; higher is better and – denotes an unreported result. Bold scores mark the best among open-weight baselines and our configurations, including the GPT-6-assisted configuration. The separate row groups distinguish closed-source baselines, open-weight baselines, and our systems. Parameter counts describe the reported generator scale; 30B-A3B denotes 30B total and 3B activated parameters. The agent-assisted rows do not specify a total system parameter count.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T6" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S6.T6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 6</span>: </span><span id="S6.T6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Compositional generation and prompt following. GenEval2 reports Soft-TIFA GM; UniGenBench++ reports English short- and long-prompt scores. Both agentic configurations use the same image generator as the standalone model.</span></figcaption>

</figure>
<section id="S6.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">6.2.1 </span>Composition and Prompt Following</h4>

<div id="S6.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We test compositional adherence with GenEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ghosh et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and GenEval2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kamath et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and semantic consistency across prompt lengths with UniGenBench++ <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib110" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>. We report GenEval2 Soft-TIFA GM and the English short and long UniGenBench++ settings. The GenEval2 source calls Nano Banana Pro Gemini 3 Pro Image, marked by <math id="S6.SS2.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dagger" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>†</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dagger</annotation></semantics></math> in Table <a href="#S6.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 6.2 Raster Image Generation and Agentic Creation ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The Nemotron-family workflow increases GenEval from 80.97 to 86.40 and GenEval2 from 31.71 to 52.56, with UniGenBench++ gains of 11.14 and 4.82 points on short and long prompts. The GPT-6-assisted configuration reaches 92.86, 65.43, 93.20, and 94.25, respectively. Its UniGenBench++ scores are close to Nano Banana Pro’s 92.72 and 94.20, while its GenEval2 score remains below GPT Image 2’s 81.00. The agentic gains support improved constraint satisfaction, with substantial variation across benchmarks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">6.2.2 </span>Visual Text Rendering</h4>

<div id="S6.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">LongTextBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Geng et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and CVTG-2K <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib98" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tai et al., 2025</a>)</cite> probe the rendering of visible text, including long strings and complex arrangements. This category concerns text inside the generated image; UniGenBench++’s long setting instead refers to the length of the input prompt.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S6.T7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 7</span>: </span><span id="S6.T7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Visual text rendering on LongTextBench and CVTG-2K, using their English settings. </figure>
<div id="S6.SS2.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The standalone raster image generator scores 94.30 on LongTextBench-EN and 84.11 on CVTG-2K-EN. Nemotron-family agents raise these to 97.00 and 89.63, and GPT-6 agents to 97.98 and 92.53. The larger gains on CVTG-2K indicate more room for improvement on its complex text requirements. SenseNova-U1.5 remains ahead of both configurations at 98.80 and 94.80, so stronger agent-assisted text rendering does not establish a lead on these benchmarks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">6.2.3 </span>Broad Visual Generation</h4>

<div id="S6.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OneIG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and Qwen-Image-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026a</a>)</cite> cover multiple aspects of visual generation. OneIG spans alignment, text, reasoning, style, and diversity; Qwen-Image-Bench includes real-world fidelity and creative generation. We group their English scores here because they summarize broader capabilities than the focused tests above.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T8" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S6.T8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 8</span>: </span><span id="S6.T8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Broad visual-generation evaluation on OneIG and Qwen-Image-Bench, using their English settings. Both agentic configurations use the same image generator as the standalone model.</span></figcaption>

<td id="S6.T8.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Params</span></td>
<td id="S6.T8.5.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">OneIG-EN <math id="S6.T8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math></span></td>

<tr id="S6.T8.5.25" class="ltx_tr">

<span id="S6.T8.5.25.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="S6.T8.5.25.1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.25.1.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation</span></span></span>
<span id="S6.T8.5.25.1.2.1.2" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S6.T8.5.25.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.25.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">-</span></td>
<td id="S6.T8.5.25.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.25.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">54.14</span></td>
<td id="S6.T8.5.25.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.25.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">51.33</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S6.T8.5.26" class="ltx_tr">

<span id="S6.T8.5.26.1.2.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">
<span id="S6.T8.5.26.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="S6.T8.5.26.1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.26.1.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation</span></span></span>
<span id="S6.T8.5.26.1.2.1.2" class="ltx_tr">

</span></span><span id="S6.T8.5.26.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"><span id="S6.T8.5.26.1.3.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></td>
<td id="S6.T8.5.26.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.26.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">-</span></td>
<td id="S6.T8.5.26.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.26.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">54.63</span></td>
<td id="S6.T8.5.26.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.26.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">52.46</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS2.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Nemotron-family agents raise OneIG from 52.77 to 54.14 and Qwen-Image-Bench from 46.36 to 51.33; GPT-6 agents reach 54.63 and 52.46. These gains are smaller than the improvements on GenEval2 and the knowledge benchmarks below. Both configurations remain below Nano Banana Pro on these two scores, and below ERNIE-Image with prompt enhancement on OneIG. The results show that better constraint handling leaves a gap on broader visual-generation criteria.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">6.2.4 </span>Knowledge and Reasoning</h4>

<div id="S6.SS2.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">WISE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib70" title="" class="ltx_ref">Niu et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> tests the use of knowledge and reasoning in visual creation. WISE follows the Verified protocol, using Qwen3.5-35B-A3B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib83" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2026</a>)</cite> to evaluate binary world-knowledge correctness on the verified prompt set.</p>
</div>
