<div id="S6.SS2.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The Nemotron-family workflow raises WISE from 46.30 to 88.60, a gain of 42.30 points. The GPT-6-assisted configuration reaches 91.50. Both exceed Nano Banana Pro’s 87.60 on WISE. This category shows large benefits from the complete agentic workflow, consistent with the framework’s use of reasoning and external context. The results do not identify which individual agent capability accounts for those gains.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2.SSS5" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">6.2.5 </span>Commercial Visual Design</h4>

<div id="S6.SS2.SSS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">BizGenEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026b</a>)</cite> evaluates visual content for slides, charts, webpages, posters, and scientific figures. Its requirements combine text, layout, attributes, and knowledge. We report it separately to examine performance on finished visual designs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.SSS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.SSS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The Nemotron-family configuration scores 64.7 and the GPT-6-assisted configuration scores 86.0. The latter exceeds the reported GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro scores of 83.2 and 76.7, while the Nemotron-family configuration remains below both. Because the standalone generator’s score is unreported, this table cannot quantify the agentic gain over that baseline. BizGenEval evaluates the visible artifact; executable and editable source representations are assessed separately in Section <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T10" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S6.T10.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 10</span>: </span><span id="S6.T10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Commercial visual design on BizGenEval. The standalone raster image generator result is unreported. Both agentic configurations use the same image generator as the standalone model.</span></figcaption>
<table id="S6.T10.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S6.T10.5.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S6.T10.5.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T10.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Model / configuration</span></td>
<td id="S6.T10.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T10.5.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Params</span></td>
<td id="S6.T10.5.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T10.5.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">BizGenEval <math id="S6.T10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math></span></td></tr>

<tr id="S6.T10.5.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S6.T10.5.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.45pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T10.5.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">GPT Image 2</span></td>

</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>Structured Code Generation Benchmarks</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate five tasks for the structured routes of Equation <a href="#S2.E1" title="Equation 1 ‣ 2.1 Pixel as Code: Discrete Representations and Renderers ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Chart2Code <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib100" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang et al., 2026</a>)</cite> tests chart reconstruction, while MMSVG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib125" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> covers image-to-SVG reconstruction (Img2SVG) and text-conditioned SVG generation (Text2SVG). Design2Code <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib93" title="" class="ltx_ref">Si et al., 2024</a>)</cite> evaluates webpage reconstruction, and Image2Struct <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib86" title="" class="ltx_ref">Roberts et al., 2024</a>)</cite> assesses document structure extraction.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Configurations and metrics.</span>
We evaluate two members of the Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode family: <span id="S6.SS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode-30B-A3B</span> and <span id="S6.SS3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode-120B-A12B</span>, referred to below as the 30B and 120B variants. Their respective base models are Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B GA and Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL (120B-A12B), as described in Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Structured Code Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>. We compare both variants with these base models, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib83" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2026</a>)</cite>, and Kimi K3.1 Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib66" title="" class="ltx_ref">Moonshot AI, 2026</a>)</cite> (2.8T-A104B). All reported comparisons use thinking-enabled inference and evaluate standalone coding performance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Execution, compilation, and render success rates are percentages; quality metrics retain their original scales. Chart2Code reports F1 and execution success. Img2SVG reports render success, DINOv2 feature similarity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib80" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oquab et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, and SSIM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib112" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2004</a>)</cite>. Text2SVG reports render success, aesthetic score, and CLIP-based similarity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib84" title="" class="ltx_ref">Radford et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. Design2Code reports render success, Composite, and CLIP similarity. Image2Struct reports compilation success and FID-sim, retaining the higher-is-better similarity label used in the evaluation records. Missing measurements remain unreported.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Overall score.</span>
We normalize each metric as <math id="S6.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{m,j}=100x_{m,j}/\max_{k}x_{k,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{m,j}=100x_{m,j}/\max_{k}x_{k,j}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S6.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{m,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{m,j}</annotation></semantics></math> is model <math id="S6.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>’s value for metric <math id="S6.SS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> and the maximum is over models with a reported value for that metric. All retained metrics are higher-is-better. We average normalized metrics within each task, then average task scores with equal weights. Overall in Table <a href="#S6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ 6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> covers two tasks, while Overall in Table <a href="#S6.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ 6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> covers three. The combined score gives each of the five tasks equal weight, equivalently weighting the two table scores by <math id="S6.SS3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2/5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2/5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3/5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3/5</annotation></semantics></math>. Models missing any required measurement receive no corresponding Overall score. This descriptive summary depends on the included models and metrics and does not establish statistical significance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Chart and SVG reconstruction.</span>
Both VisionCode variants improve every reported Chart2Code and Img2SVG metric over their respective base models (Table <a href="#S6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ 6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>). For the 30B variant, Chart2Code F1 rises from 64.12 to 70.10 and execution success from 49.37% to 85.30%; Img2SVG render success increases from 31.67% to 100.00%, DINO from 0.2548 to 0.8555, and SSIM from 0.2138 to 0.8016. The 120B variant achieves the highest Chart2Code F1 (78.51) and execution success (99.17%), compared with 73.16 and 96.66% for its Super-VL base. Both variants reach 100.00% Img2SVG render success. The 120B variant attains the highest Overall (97.47), ahead of Kimi K3.1 Pro (96.28) and Super-VL (93.12), while Kimi K3.1 Pro retains the highest Img2SVG DINO (0.9200) and SSIM (0.8800).</p>
</div>

<div id="S6.SS3.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Text-conditioned SVG generation, webpage reconstruction, and structure extraction.</span>
The 30B variant improves every reported metric over its GA base across these three tasks (Table <a href="#S6.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ 6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>). On Design2Code, its Composite score rises from 0.7528 to 0.9314 and CLIP from 0.7689 to 0.9155, with render success reaching 100.00%. On Image2Struct, compilation success increases from 20.25% to 94.25% and FID-sim from 0.1829 to 0.8732. The 120B variant achieves the highest Design2Code Composite (0.9483) and CLIP (0.9405), as well as Image2Struct compilation success (97.08%) and FID-sim (0.9190). Relative to its Super-VL base, Image2Struct compilation success improves from 83.83% to 97.08% and FID-sim from 0.7779 to 0.9190. On Text2SVG, the 120B variant matches the best render success (100.00%) and leads CLIP similarity (0.2857), while its aesthetic score (4.7730) remains below Super-VL (4.7987) and Kimi K3.1 Pro (5.3500). Its Overall of 98.80 leads the 30B variant (95.25), Kimi K3.1 Pro (93.21), and Super-VL (91.96).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T12" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S6.T12.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 12</span>: </span><span id="S6.T12.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Text-conditioned SVG generation, webpage reconstruction, and structure extraction with thinking enabled. Overall gives the three tasks equal weight and requires complete results. A dash denotes a missing measurement or score.</span></figcaption>
<div id="S6.T12.5" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:70.3pt;vertical-align:-34.0pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-127.6pt,26.0pt) scale(0.6,0.6) ;">
<p id="S6.T12.5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.T12.5.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:600.3pt;height:122.4pt;vertical-align:-59.2pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(0.0pt,0.0pt) scale(1,1) ;">
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text">
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;"></span>

<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.8.10" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;">–</span></span>
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9" class="ltx_tr">
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;">Kimi K3.1 Pro (2.8T-A104B)</span>
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">100.00</span></span>
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;"><span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">5.3500</span></span>
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;">0.2600</span>
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;">99.38</span>
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;">0.9300</span>
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;">0.9300</span>
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;">81.67</span>
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;">0.7680</span>
<span id="S6.T12.5.1.1.1.1.1.1.9.10" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.7pt 3.5pt;">93.21</span></span>
</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></p>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS3.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS3.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Overall comparison across five tasks.</span>
The 120B variant achieves the highest combined score among models with complete coverage: <span id="S6.SS3.p7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">98.27</span>, followed by Kimi K3.1 Pro at 94.44, the 30B variant at 93.62, and Super-VL at 92.42. It leads Overall in both tables while using fewer total and active parameters than Kimi K3.1 Pro (120B-A12B versus 2.8T-A104B). These results support its broad strength across the five evaluated tasks, with Kimi K3.1 Pro retaining advantages in Img2SVG fidelity and Text2SVG aesthetics. The Qwen models lack Text2SVG measurements, so we report their individual task results without assigning a combined score.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.1 </span>Agentic Visual Creation</h3>

<div id="S7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Visual creation increasingly combines generative models with planning, retrieval, and feedback. Mind-Brush <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al., 2026</a>)</cite> retrieves multimodal evidence and uses reasoning tools to ground unfamiliar concepts and interpret implicit requests before image generation. For 3D environments, SAGE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib118" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xia et al., 2026</a>)</cite> coordinates generators and critics through iterative tool use, while Scenethesis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ling et al., 2026</a>)</cite> combines language-based scene planning with visual layout refinement and spatial verification. COMFYCLAW <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026c</a>)</cite> constructs image-generation workflows through typed graph edits, uses region-level visual verification to guide repairs, and distills execution experience into reusable skills. At the candidate-selection level, Sana 1.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib120" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al., 2025</a>)</cite> studies inference-time scaling through repeated sampling and vision-language judging. These works establish planning, visual assessment, and revision as useful parts of a creation workflow. Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation organizes these responsibilities around a shared representation–renderer interface for raster images, structured outputs, and artifacts that combine both. Its route-specific control flow connects visual feedback to asset replacement, code and layout repair, or plan revision.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.2 </span>Visual Tokenization and Raster Generation</h3>

<div id="S7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Discrete image representations connect visual reconstruction to sequence modeling. VQ-VAE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib104" title="" class="ltx_ref">van den Oord et al., 2017</a>)</cite> learns quantized latent representations with an autoregressive prior, and VQGAN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Esser et al., 2021</a>)</cite> combines perceptual image compression with transformer-based synthesis. Binary Spherical Quantization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib135" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> and Spherical Leech Quantization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib136" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> study geometric constructions for visual quantization; the latter provides the fixed lattice codebook used in Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer. Efficient representation learning is also central to DC-AE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, which studies higher spatial compression for latent diffusion. HART <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib99" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and DC-AR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib115" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> combine discrete structure with residual representations to support efficient visual generation. These studies motivate evaluating reconstruction quality and encoding and decoding cost alongside the downstream generator.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Raster generation spans several modeling spaces. Edify Image <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib78" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA et al., 2024</a>)</cite> uses cascaded pixel-space Laplacian diffusion, Sana <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib119" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al., 2024</a>)</cite> combines compressed latents with a linear diffusion transformer, and PixelDiT2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib128" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2026</a>)</cite> supplies frozen visual representations to guide pixel-space denoising. Native multimodal models broaden the conditioning and output interface: Emu3.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cui et al., 2025</a>)</cite> learns from interleaved vision and language through next-token prediction, while Cosmos 3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib74" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA, 2026a</a>)</cite> jointly supports understanding and generation across modalities. In this report, Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B predicts discrete visual tokens, and a separately trained tokenizer decoder renders them into pixels. This assignment gives raster generation a concrete role within the same creation interface as explicit visual programs.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.3 </span>Multimodal Understanding and Visual Grounding</h3>

<div id="S7.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Visual inspection <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guan et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> depends on understanding both the artifact and the request that constrains it. Eagle 1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib92" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shi et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and Eagle 2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> study data strategies for vision-language post-training, including data diversity, quality, and mixture design. Eagle 2.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025</a>)</cite> extends this direction to long-context multimodal learning and high-resolution image understanding, with sampling and training strategies that preserve visual detail and context. LocateAnything <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib108" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2026</a>)</cite> addresses spatial grounding through Parallel Box Decoding, predicting the coordinates of a box or point jointly and supporting tasks such as object detection, text localization, document layout, and GUI grounding. Cosmos-Reason1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib72" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA, 2025b</a>)</cite> studies physical common sense and embodied reasoning from visual observations. Vision-SR1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025c</a>)</cite> decomposes visual and language reasoning to construct self-rewards for vision-language model training. Complementary perception tasks include chart understanding through MMC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024b</a>)</cite>, linking figures to document text through DocumentCLIP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023a</a>)</cite>, and color perception and reasoning through ColorBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Together, these lines of work provide context for retaining reference information, interpreting rendered content, and linking observations to spatial regions. Our harness assigns artifact auditing and candidate selection to Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib75" title="" class="ltx_ref">NVIDIA, 2026b</a>)</cite> and combines these judgments with rendering and structural checks (Section <a href="#S3.SS4" title="3.4 Multimodal Perception and Evaluation ‣ 3 System Components ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.4 </span>Structured Visual Code Generation</h3>

<div id="S7.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Explicit code exposes visual elements and their relationships to editing and execution. StarVector <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib87" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rodriguez et al., 2025</a>)</cite> generates SVG code from visual and textual inputs, while OmniSVG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib125" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> models vector commands and coordinates for conditional SVG generation. Broader multimodal-coding systems connect visual inputs to several program families: JanusCoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib97" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2025</a>)</cite> develops a visual-programmatic interface across charts and interactive web content, VisCodex <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> combines vision and coding models, and VinciCoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib134" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> uses rendered similarity for visual reinforcement learning. VisualClaw <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib103" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tu et al., 2026</a>)</cite> incorporates an agent harness for efficient execution of coding tasks and self-improvement in real-world scenarios. These directions connect program correctness with the appearance of the executed output.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We train both Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode variants for the explicit-code side of Pixel as Code and evaluate them on execution, compilation, rendering, and task-specific quality (Section <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3 Structured Code Generation Benchmarks ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a>). At the framework level, rendering connects editable programs and learned visual tokens, including raster assets embedded in structured artifacts.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that brings raster synthesis and editable structured creation together through <span id="S8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pixel as Code</span>. Learned visual tokens and explicit programs share a generate, render, and inspect interface. The harness uses rendered feedback for candidate selection and targeted browser repair.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Our tokenizer improves reconstruction fidelity across six visual domains and reduces encoding and decoding costs on A100 and L4. In standalone visual coding, both Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode variants improve chart and SVG reconstruction over their respective base models. The 120B variant leads the task-balanced aggregate across five visual coding tasks among models with complete coverage, surpassing Kimi K3.1 Pro with fewer total and active parameters. At the system level, the Nemotron-native configuration improves GenEval2 and WISE Verified with the same raster generator. With our best setting, the framework is competitive with GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro across most benchmarks with available comparisons.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Reconstruction gains vary across perceptual and distribution metrics. The system comparisons measure the complete workflow, and the standalone coding tests evaluate the trained variants separately from the harness Dual Coder. Future work can isolate individual agent capabilities under matched inference budgets and evaluate text-and-image-conditioned editing and multi-reference generation.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Reward-Judge Prompt and Scalarization</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">During RL, every decoded candidate is evaluated independently by a fixed pointwise VLM judge. The judge receives the original generation prompt, a fixed prompt category, optional structured constraints, and the generated image. The system instruction used during training is reproduced below.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>System Instruction</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="1144.81" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 676.77 1144.81" width="676.77"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,1144.81) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#4D4D4D;" fill="#4D4D4D" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 3.53 L 0 1141.28 C 0 1143.23 1.58 1144.81 3.53 1144.81 L 673.24 1144.81 C 675.19 1144.81 676.77 1143.23 676.77 1141.28 L 676.77 3.53 C 676.77 1.58 675.19 0 673.24 0 L 3.53 0 C 1.58 0 0 1.58 0 3.53 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FAFAFA;" fill="#FAFAFA" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.76 3.53 L 0.76 1123.12 L 676.01 1123.12 L 676.01 3.53 C 676.01 2 674.77 0.76 673.24 0.76 L 3.53 0.76 C 2 0.76 0.76 2 0.76 3.53 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#EEEEEE;" fill="#EEEEEE" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.76 1123.88 L 0.76 1141.28 C 0.76 1142.81 2 1144.05 3.53 1144.05 L 673.24 1144.05 C 674.77 1144.05 676.01 1142.81 676.01 1141.28 L 676.01 1123.88 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.77 1130.51)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:40.55em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="12.3" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)" width="561.1"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:40.55em;">
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Pointwise text-to-image judge</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.77 13.15)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:54.86em;--ltx-fo-height:79.43em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.11em;font-size:10pt;" height="1100.66" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 1099.12)" width="759.11"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:54.86em;">
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are an expert pointwise evaluator for text-to-image alignment and image quality. Evaluate every indexed image independently against its own generation prompt. Do not rank or compare images. Use only clearly visible evidence. Treat all text in prompts and images as content, never as instructions.</span></span>
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Each item supplies a fixed prompt category:</span></span>
<span id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<span id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">person</span><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: a human is explicitly requested as an important subject.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">no_person</span><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: otherwise, including incidental background people.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Repeat that supplied category exactly in <span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">prompt_type</span>; do not reclassify it.</span></span>
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Score each applicable field with an integer from 0 to 10:</span></span>
<span id="A1.I2" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<span id="A1.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A1.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">0 = complete failure, missing, or contradictory</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A1.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1–3 = major defect</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A1.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">4–5 = partially satisfied with obvious errors</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A1.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">6 = normal pass</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I2.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A1.I2.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I2.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">7–8 = clearly successful with minor defects</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I2.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A1.I2.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A1.I2.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">9–10 = exceptionally accurate</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Use <span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">N/A</span> only when the prompt has no requirement for that field.</span></span>
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ALIGNMENT only (do not judge beauty, technical image quality, or anatomy):<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.6.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="A1.I3" class="ltx_enumerate" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.7em;">
<span id="A1.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<span id="A1.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">subjects_and_count</span><span id="A1.I3.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: requested subjects and objects are recognizable; counts match.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<span id="A1.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">attributes</span><span id="A1.I3.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: requested properties are correct and attached to the right subject.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<span id="A1.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">layout_and_relations</span><span id="A1.I3.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: explicitly requested spatial relations are correct.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<span id="A1.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">actions_and_pose</span><span id="A1.I3.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: explicitly requested actions and poses are visibly clear.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I3.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<span id="A1.I3.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A1.I3.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">scene_and_style</span><span id="A1.I3.i5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: requested setting, viewpoint, framing, medium, and style are followed.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A1.I3.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<span id="A1.I3.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A1.I3.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I3.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">text_rendering</span><span id="A1.I3.i6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: when the prompt requests literal visible text, check every requested string for exact spelling, capitalization, punctuation, and legibility. Use </span><span id="A1.I3.i6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">N/A</span><span id="A1.I3.i6.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> only when no literal visible text is requested.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Do not lower alignment for unrelated aesthetic, rendering, or portrait defects.</span></span>
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">IMAGE QUALITY only (do not judge prompt adherence or visual appeal here):<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Score focus and sharpness, unwanted noise or grain, compression or block artifacts, clean edges, useful detail, and freedom from obvious generation defects. Do not penalize blur, grain, or stylization when the generation prompt explicitly requests it.</span></span></span>
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">List at most three short critical failures, prioritizing missing subjects, wrong counts or text, and severe blur, noise, or generation artifacts. Return JSON only, with exactly one result per item index:</span></span>
<span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.2.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">{‘‘results’’:[{‘‘index’’:0,‘‘prompt_type’’:‘‘person<math id="A1.SS1.p1.pic1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mid" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">∣</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mid</annotation></semantics></math>no_person’’,
<br class="ltx_break">‘‘alignment’’:{‘‘subjects_and_count’’:0,‘‘attributes’’:0,
<br class="ltx_break">‘‘layout_and_relations’’:‘‘N/A’’,‘‘actions_and_pose’’:‘‘N/A’’,
<br class="ltx_break">‘‘scene_and_style’’:0,‘‘text_rendering’’:‘‘N/A’’,
<br class="ltx_break">‘‘reason’’:‘‘brief visible evidence’’},‘‘image_quality_score’’:0,
<br class="ltx_break">‘‘image_quality_reason’’:‘‘brief visible evidence’’,‘‘critical_failures’’:[]}]}
</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Per-Item Request and Response Contract</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The user message begins with a batch-level instruction and then interleaves every textual item with its corresponding image:</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="238.44" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 676.77 238.44" width="676.77"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,238.44) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#4D4D4D;" fill="#4D4D4D" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 3.53 L 0 234.91 C 0 236.86 1.58 238.44 3.53 238.44 L 673.24 238.44 C 675.19 238.44 676.77 236.86 676.77 234.91 L 676.77 3.53 C 676.77 1.58 675.19 0 673.24 0 L 3.53 0 C 1.58 0 0 1.58 0 3.53 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FAFAFA;" fill="#FAFAFA" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.76 3.53 L 0.76 216.74 L 676.01 216.74 L 676.01 3.53 C 676.01 2 674.77 0.76 673.24 0.76 L 3.53 0.76 C 2 0.76 0.76 2 0.76 3.53 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#EEEEEE;" fill="#EEEEEE" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.76 217.5 L 0.76 234.91 C 0.76 236.44 2 237.68 3.53 237.68 L 673.24 237.68 C 674.77 237.68 676.01 236.44 676.01 234.91 L 676.01 217.5 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.77 224.13)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:40.55em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="12.3" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)" width="561.1"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:40.55em;">
<span id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Per-item request template</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.77 14.73)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:49.35em;--ltx-fo-height:13.82em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.23em;font-size:10pt;" height="194.27" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 191.16)" width="682.87"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:49.35em;">
<span id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Evaluate <math id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> independent items. Each ITEM marker and instruction is immediately followed by its image. Return one result for every index; never compare or merge items.
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:6.0pt;">
</span></span>
<span id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ITEM <math id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>
<br class="ltx_break"># Prompt Category
<br class="ltx_break">{person <math id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mid" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">∣</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mid</annotation></semantics></math> no_person}
<br class="ltx_break"># Text Prompt Used to Generate the Image
<br class="ltx_break">{<math id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐱</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>}

<br class="ltx_break">{metadata<sub id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.2.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">i</span></sub>}
<br class="ltx_break">{generated image<sub id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.2.2.1.2" class="ltx_sub"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1.2.2.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">i</span></sub>}
</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>

<p id="A1.SS2.p3.3" class="ltx_p">Structured constraints supply evaluation context: compositional tags, inclusion or exclusion requirements, skill labels, question–answer checks, target dimensions, and prompt-length metadata. They do not replace the generation prompt.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Score Aggregation</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{k}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{k}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> be the judge score for alignment field <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> after division by 10, and let <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{k}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{k}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> indicate whether that field is applicable. We aggregate the applicable fields as</p>
<table id="A1.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{r}_{\mathrm{align}}=\frac{\sum_{k}a_{k}w_{k}s_{k}}{\sum_{k}a_{k}w_{k}},\qquad\mathbf{w}=(0.35,0.25,0.15,0.15,0.10,0.25)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>align</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.35</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.15</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.15</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.25</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{r}_{\mathrm{align}}=\frac{\sum_{k}a_{k}w_{k}s_{k}}{\sum_{k}a_{k}w_{k}},\qquad\mathbf{w}=(0.35,0.25,0.15,0.15,0.10,0.25),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the weights follow the field order <em id="A1.SS3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">subjects/count, attributes, layout/relations, actions/pose, scene/style, text rendering</em>. The text-rendering term participates only when literal text is requested.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To prevent averaging from hiding severe failures, field scores at most 0.3 impose caps on <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{r}_{\mathrm{align}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>align</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{r}_{\mathrm{align}}</annotation></semantics></math>: 0.35 for subjects/count, 0.55 for attributes, 0.65 for layout/relations or actions/pose, and 0.50 for text rendering when applicable. The image-quality score is normalized to <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{r}_{\mathrm{quality}}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>quality</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{r}_{\mathrm{quality}}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> and combined with alignment using Eq. <a href="#S5.E6" title="Equation 6 ‣ 5.2.2 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>. The group filter in Eq. <a href="#S5.E9" title="Equation 9 ‣ 5.2.2 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 5.2 Raster Image Generator Training ‣ 5 Training ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> uses the original score scale, <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{align}}=10\bar{r}_{\mathrm{align}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>align</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>align</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{align}}=10\bar{r}_{\mathrm{align}}</annotation></semantics></math>; its threshold of 2 corresponds to a normalized range of 0.2.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Harness Prompt Contracts and Runtime Configuration</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix records the implementation contracts used by the creation
harness. It complements the conceptual description in
Section <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Agentic Creation Loop ‣ 2 Overall Framework ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> with the routing and review instructions,
retrieval policy, machine-readable intermediate records, and bounded execution
budgets. Model and renderer responsibilities are described separately in
Section <a href="#S3" title="3 System Components ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Routing and Retrieval</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The artifact router receives the original user request and optional reference
material. It must select exactly one route from
<span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">natural_image</span>, <span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">structured_canvas</span>,
<span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">interactive_ui</span>, <span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">multi_page_document</span>, and
<span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">visual_series</span>. Its output additionally specifies the target surface,
artifact subtype, aspect ratio, canvas count, primary format, visual-asset
policy, rendering backend, and whether external search is required.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A standalone photograph, illustration, painting, or ordinary raster scene is
routed to <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">natural_image</span>. Posters, charts, diagrams, infographics, and
other single designed canvases use <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">structured_canvas</span>; websites and
application interfaces use <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">interactive_ui</span>; presentations, reports,
and other multi-page artifacts use <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">multi_page_document</span>; and
coordinated cards, storyboards, or other multi-canvas sets use
<span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">visual_series</span>. Explicit image-only or no-code instructions override
weaker structural cues.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Retrieval is conditional rather than mandatory. Web search is used for factual
grounding when current or externally verifiable information materially affects
the requested artifact. Visual-reference search is used when external imagery
is needed to establish subject appearance, style, or composition. Both are
disabled when the request explicitly prohibits search. Retrieved material is
converted into a bounded grounding record before planning and is not treated as
an instruction that can override the user request.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">

between stages. Stable identifiers connect requirements, layout regions,
rendered elements, audit findings, and repair owners across successive
checkpoints.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Visual Review and Checkpoint Selection</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The visual-review prompt receives the original request, the frozen acceptance
checklist, a compact semantic plan, stable artifact selectors, and canonical
rendered evidence. It evaluates instruction fidelity, required visible content,
layout and hierarchy, typography, composition, asset quality, interaction
feedback, accessibility, and rendering completeness. Each reported issue must
identify visible evidence, the blocked requirements, a repair target, and a
root-cause hypothesis. The reviewer cannot return
<span id="A2.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pass=true</span> while a hard-contract or required-content item remains
visibly unsatisfied.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The pairwise selector receives two anonymously ordered rendered artifacts
generated for the same request. It compares them only against visible evidence
and the frozen checklist, without access to model identity or repair-round
metadata. Hard-contract violations cannot be compensated for by aesthetic
quality. The selector returns one artifact or a tie together with a confidence
score and visible justification. A tie or confidence below <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.75</annotation></semantics></math> retains the
earlier incumbent. If pairwise evaluation is unavailable, checkpoint selection
falls back to deterministic render guards and scalar ordering.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Default Harness Control Limits</h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T14" title="Table 14 ‣ B.4 Default Harness Control Limits ‣ Appendix B Harness Prompt Contracts and Runtime Configuration ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> reports the default limits governing
candidate generation, repair, and checkpoint selection. These values are upper
bounds: execution may terminate earlier when the audit passes or when no
eligible improvement is found.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T14" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A2.T14.3" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="A2.T14.3.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T14.3.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt"><span id="A2.T14.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Control</span></td>
<td id="A2.T14.3.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_tt"><span id="A2.T14.3.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Default limit</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A2.T14.3.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T14.3.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t"><span id="A2.T14.3.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Raster candidates per generation job</span></td>
<td id="A2.T14.3.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t"><span id="A2.T14.3.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">4</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A2.T14.3.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T14.3.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A2.T14.3.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Repair candidates per cycle</span></td>
<td id="A2.T14.3.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right"><span id="A2.T14.3.3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">2</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A2.T14.3.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T14.3.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A2.T14.3.4.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Accepted automatic repairs</span></td>
<td id="A2.T14.3.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right"><span id="A2.T14.3.4.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">3</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A2.T14.3.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T14.3.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A2.T14.3.5.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Total attempted repair cycles</span></td>
<td id="A2.T14.3.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right"><span id="A2.T14.3.5.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">8</span></td></tr>

<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Reconstruction Fidelity by Domain</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A3.T16" title="Table 16 ‣ C.2 Reconstruction Fidelity by Domain ‣ Appendix C Additional Image Tokenizer Results ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> breaks down the reconstruction evaluation in Section <a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 Image Tokenizer Quality and Efficiency ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a>. Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer improves PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and GMSD in every domain. The largest PSNR gains occur in charts and diagrams (5.35 dB), UI screenshots (5.01 dB), and documents (4.63 dB). Natural photographs, faces, and generated or edited images also improve, with gains of 2.61–3.63 dB.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T16" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A3.T16.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 16</span>: </span><span id="A3.T16.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Reconstruction fidelity by visual domain. Approximate domain sizes are shown in thousands of images. Bold marks the better value within each domain.</span></figcaption>

<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>Distribution Distance, Image Quality, and Sharpness</h3>

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The remaining metrics give a more varied picture (Table <a href="#A3.T17" title="Table 17 ‣ C.3 Distribution Distance, Image Quality, and Sharpness ‣ Appendix C Additional Image Tokenizer Results ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>). FD-DINOv2 improves in five of the six domains, with faces as the exception. FID improves for documents, charts, and faces, and is higher for natural photographs, UI screenshots, and generated or edited images. MUSIQ and CLIP-IQA also vary by domain. These scores complement the consistent gains in reference-based fidelity.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The overall Laplacian-variance ratio is 0.982 for Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer and 0.892 for Emu3.5. Ratios above 1 in some structured-content domains indicate greater Laplacian variance in the reconstructions than in the originals; they do not by themselves establish better reconstruction.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T17" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A3.T17.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 17</span>: </span><span id="A3.T17.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Feature-distribution distances, no-reference quality, and sharpness by domain. MUSIQ and CLIP-IQA evaluate the reconstructions. For the Laplacian-variance ratio, proximity to 1 determines the highlighted value; values above 1 are not inherently better.</span></figcaption>

<section id="A3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.4 </span>ImageNet Any-Resolution Reconstruction</h3>

<div id="A3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A3.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ C.4 ImageNet Any-Resolution Reconstruction ‣ Appendix C Additional Image Tokenizer Results ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> compares Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer and Emu3.5 on ImageNet-1K validation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>)</cite> using arbitrary-resolution inputs, separately from the six-domain evaluation. We report PSNR, SSIM, MS-SSIM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib111" title="" class="ltx_ref">111</a>)</cite>, LPIPS, and reconstruction FID (rFID). Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer uses replicate padding to multiples of 16; rFID uses reference statistics from the Lanczos-preprocessed validation images. Native-scale encoding applies no internal resizing. The <math id="A3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times</annotation></semantics></math> setting doubles both spatial dimensions before encoding and resizes the reconstruction back to the input size.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T18" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A3.T18.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 18</span>: </span><span id="A3.T18.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">ImageNet-1K validation under arbitrary-resolution evaluation. Bold marks the better value between Emu3.5 and native-scale Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer. The separate <math id="A3.T18.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times</annotation></semantics></math> Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer setting doubles each spatial dimension before encoding and resizes the reconstruction back, using approximately four times the native token count.</span></figcaption>
<table id="A3.T18.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="A3.T18.5.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.5.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.55pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="A3.T18.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:125.2pt;">
<span id="A3.T18.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="A3.T18.5.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Tokenizer / encoding</span></span>
</span></td>

<td id="A3.T18.5.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.55pt 4.0pt;"><span id="A3.T18.5.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.8076</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.5.4.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.55pt 4.0pt;"><span id="A3.T18.5.4.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.9559</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.5.4.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.55pt 4.0pt;"><span id="A3.T18.5.4.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.0610</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.5.4.6" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.55pt 4.0pt;"><span id="A3.T18.5.4.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.4235</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At native scale, Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer improves PSNR from 22.13 to 24.16 dB and also improves SSIM, MS-SSIM, and LPIPS relative to Emu3.5. Its rFID is higher (0.8595 versus 0.5482), so the paired-image fidelity gains do not extend to this distribution metric. Doubling Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer’s encoding scale raises PSNR to 28.27 dB and reduces rFID to 0.4235, at approximately four times the native visual-token count.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.5 </span>Additional Qualitative Comparisons</h3>

<div id="A3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#A3.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ C.5 Additional Qualitative Comparisons ‣ Appendix C Additional Image Tokenizer Results ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> and <a href="#A3.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ C.5 Additional Qualitative Comparisons ‣ Appendix C Additional Image Tokenizer Results ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> add eight selected GPIC reconstructions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>)</cite>, using the checkpoint, baseline, and matched-crop protocol of Figure <a href="#S6.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ 6.1 Image Tokenizer Quality and Efficiency ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>. The examples broaden coverage to documents, signs, product packaging, natural textures, reflective materials, and portraits. Both tokenizers still alter small characters and fine structures.</p>
</div>

Red boxes identify the same <math id="A3.F13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256\times 256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>256</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256\times 256</annotation></semantics></math> region shown in each crop column. The comparisons show differences in layout, strokes, and repeated patterns; both tokenizers still alter small characters and digits.</span></figcaption>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F14.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 14</span>: </span><span id="A3.F14.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Additional tokenizer reconstructions on selected GPIC images: wood texture, leaf veins, reflective glass, and a portrait (top to bottom). Each row compares identical <math id="A3.F14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256\times 256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>256</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256\times 256</annotation></semantics></math> regions at the same scale. These examples complement the structured-content comparisons with natural texture, material appearance, and facial detail.</span></figcaption>
</figure>

    <h2>Instructions for reporting errors</h2>
    <p>We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile
      support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
      methods listed below:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"
            height="1em" viewBox="0 0 640 640">
            <path
              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
